event_data.context:
## Expected workflow and state transitions

For every individual implementation-file or test-file edit, immediately run the smallest relevant test set. Record the durable workflow state as one of: `failing`, `passing-awaiting-required-gates-or-review`, `committed`, or `pushed` (or the delivery-mode-equivalent terminal checkpoint).

- `edit -> test -> failing`: do not commit or push. Permit only the next causal edit needed to address that failure, then test immediately again.
- `edit -> test -> passing`: stop implementation/test editing; complete mechanically required gates for that exact snapshot, perform required final review in the correct sequence, create a signed commit, run exact-commit verification, and make a normal push before another implementation/test edit where the configured delivery mode allows pushing.
- `passing -> review finding -> failing-or-passing-awaiting-review`: make only the causal remediation, retest immediately, and reset/repeat review as existing policy requires.
- `committed -> exact-revision verification failure`: do not push; make a new causal change and follow the normal signed-commit sequence. Never amend without explicit authorization.
- `pushed -> continuous-integration failure`: enter the existing Tiber-owned recovery hold and follow its single-causal-repair or authorized unchanged-revision-rerun policy before new feature work.
- interruption at any point: retain a durable checkpoint that identifies the exact snapshot and its last known state (`failing`, `passing-awaiting-required-gates-or-review`, `committed`, or `pushed`) so another session can resume without guessing.

## Policy interactions

The feature belongs in `development-system:development-workflow` and must compose with, rather than replace, the existing test-driven-development, delivery, final-review, exact-revision verification, signing, continuous-integration recovery, authorization, and Tiber policies.

- Final review still precedes the commit when source-content review is required; a content-identical signed commit is followed by the existing exact-commit gate, then normal push and exact-revision continuous integration.
- Tiber remains the durable authority for active task state, review records when configured, interruption checkpoints, and pushed continuous-integration recovery holds.
- Delivery mode determines the terminal checkpoint: direct-to-trunk uses a normal push; pull-request mode uses the repository’s branch/push and pull-request lifecycle without inferring permission to open, merge, amend, force-push, or delete; local-only mode stops at the locally permitted signed checkpoint and records that no push is authorized.
- Never infer authorization to amend commits, force-push, merge, delete remote state, open a pull request when permission is required, or bypass a protected delivery boundary.

## Bounded RED-to-GREEN exception

When a test edit and its corresponding implementation edit cannot independently pass, allow one explicitly declared and tightly scoped RED-to-GREEN pair. Test immediately after the RED edit, record the expected failure and its causal claim, make only the paired implementation edit, and test immediately again. If GREEN is not reached, return to the one-causal-edit loop. Once GREEN is reached, complete review, delivery, and checkpointing immediately before any additional implementation or test change.

## Non-code and generated changes

Define explicit sequencing for documentation, configuration, formatting-only changes, and generated artifacts. Pure documentation or formatting changes may use their applicable deterministic gates instead of behavior tests, but independently passing snapshots must still be checkpointed according to delivery mode. Configuration changes use the checks that exercise the affected configuration. Generated artifacts remain coupled to the source edit that deterministically produces them and do not count as a convenience batch; regeneration and validation happen before the snapshot’s checkpoint. Mechanically required files or gates may join the snapshot only when they are consequences of the triggering edit.

## Tests

Add behavioral coverage for passing, failing, bounded RED-to-GREEN, interrupted/resumed, local-only, direct-to-trunk, and pull-request delivery modes. Tests must prove gate ordering, prohibit convenience batching after GREEN, preserve authorization boundaries, and verify durable state transitions and recovery behavior.

## Required instruction and skill changes

Update the development-workflow instructions and the retained test-driven-development and delivery workflow contracts as needed. Update final-review and Tiber instructions only where necessary to define sequencing and durable checkpoint records; do not duplicate their existing authorities. Add or update model-mediated behavior fixtures and graders because these instruction changes alter agent behavior, and bump the development-system plugin version and synchronized marketplace metadata under repository versioning policy.
event_data.summary: Development work can accumulate several independently passing changes before any durable checkpoint is created, making interruptions harder to recover from and increasing the size and risk of each delivery. Introduce a workflow rule that tests every implementation or test edit immediately and preserves each passing snapshot through the repository’s required review, commit, and delivery process before further implementation or test edits. The outcome should be small, auditable checkpoints without weakening final review, exact-revision verification, signing, continuous-integration recovery, delivery-mode, or authorization safeguards.
event_data.title: Preserve each passing development step as a delivered checkpoint
